subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — confirmation

Subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs - follow up

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo today — super helpful. A few follow-ups from our security and procurement teams around how Redwood handles PII that shows up in prompts or model outputs. Can you confirm in writing the following?

1) What user-provided prompt text and model outputs are persisted by default (full prompts, masked, metadata only)?
2) Where is any stored data physically located (region/account)?
3) Retention windows for logs, transcripts, and any cached KV/prefix data (please be explicit).
4) What logging/tracing is enabled by default (request/response logs, traces, token-level logs)?
5) Are there controls/flags (e.g., no-store, redaction) we can set per-request or per-account?
6) If we move to Dedicated or Private, can you confirm that Redwood will not persist prompts/outputs and that all traffic stays in our VPC/region?

We need a succinct written response we can share with procurement/security — preferably by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Thompson
Security & Privacy Lead
Acme Corp
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: PII handling for prompts/outputs - follow up

Emma — thanks for the note and great questions. Summary below — attaching a short dataflow diagram (redwood-pii-dataflow.png) and I'll loop in Neha for the formal attestation.

High-level answers (short):
- What we store: by default, for hosted API requests we persist request metadata (timestamp, model, route), request/response logs (prompt + output) for up to 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring. Long-term storage of raw prompts/outputs is not done unless a customer opts in (e.g., for evals or retention setting).
- Where stored: hosted data is stored in AWS regions (primary: us-east-1 for your account unless otherwise requested). We have EU regions available; data residency is configurable for enterprise accounts.
- Retention: default retention for request/response logs is 30 days. Audit logs and billing records retained longer per contract (90 days default for audit traces; can be extended). KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and not written to persistent long-term storage; they are held in-memory/ephemeral storage on serving nodes and flushed per policy.
- Logging/tracing: default includes request/response logs and high-level traces (route-level latency, error traces). We do not store token-level logs by default in persisted storage; token-level telemetry is aggregated for performance metrics only.
- Controls: yes — we offer a per-request flag (no_store=true) that prevents request/response persistence and excludes the transaction from debugging logs. You can also enable automatic redaction (PII filters) on routes to mask common PII patterns.
- Dedicated/Private: Dedicated offers reserved capacity with configurable persistence policies; we can disable request/response persistence and retain only minimal operational metrics. Private (VPC/on-prem) keeps all inference in your environment; by contract we can ensure no prompts/outputs leave your VPC and Redwood's control plane only has metadata as negotiated.

Action items / next steps I propose:
- Neha will provide formal written confirmation and the SOC2 summary attachment.
- If you need a signed attestation for procurement, Neha can provide standard language or a customer-specific addendum.
- If you want to test the no_store flag in a sandbox, I can get you credentials for a short eval.

Subject: Re: PII handling for prompts/outputs - follow up (Formal confirmation & SOC2 summary)

Hi Emma — following up with formal confirmations and the SOC 2 summary attached. See answers below (formalized):

1) Persistence scope
- Hosted API (default): We persist request metadata and request/response payloads (prompts and model outputs) for operational debugging and quality monitoring. Persistence period is configurable; default: 30 days. Customers may opt-in to longer-term storage for evals or audit purposes.
- Dedicated: Persistence is configurable per-customer. By default we retain minimal operational metrics; request/response persistence can be disabled.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): No prompts/outputs are persisted by Redwood outside the customer's environment. Storage and logs remain within customer-managed infrastructure unless otherwise contracted.

2) Physical location & residency
- Hosted: Data is stored in AWS regions. For Acme we can set residency to us-east-1 (default) or mirror to another region on request. EU residency is available for EU contracts.

3) Retention windows
- Request/response logs: default 30 days (can be reduced to 0/no-store or extended per contract).
- Audit logs/billing: default 90 days, extendable.
- KV/prefix caches: ephemeral; not persisted to durable storage.

4) Logging/tracing details
- Stored: request/response payloads (when persistence enabled), route-level traces, and aggregated telemetry.
- Not stored by default: token-level persistent logs. Token-level metrics are aggregated and anonymized for performance analysis.

5) Controls available
- Per-request no_store flag (no_store=true) — prevents persistence of request/response and excludes the call from standard debug logs.
- Account-level persistence setting — disable request/response persistence for the entire account.
- Redaction filters — automatic PII detection and masking for common patterns (SSNs, credit cards, emails).

6) Contractual guarantees for Dedicated/Private
- Dedicated: We will include a contract clause to disable persistence at the request/response level and to keep data within specified cloud regions and accounts.
- Private: All inference runs in your VPC/on-prem; Redwood will not persist prompts/outputs outside your environment.

Attachments: redwood-pii-dataflow.png (diagram), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 summary).

If you’d like, we can produce a short procurement-ready paragraph that summarizes the guarantees (1–2 paragraphs) for your contract team. Happy to provide a signed attestation template as a next step.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Trust (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
